title: Why Movie Theater Popcorn Is So Expensive
description:
Movie theaters hand studios more than half of a blockbuster ticket but keep about 82 cents of every snack dollar, and the trick goes back to the Great Depression.
#movietheater #popcorn #business #shorts

Sources: AMC Entertainment 2025 annual report and Q2 2025 10-Q; Smithsonian Magazine; Reader's Digest; NBC News/CNBC; Los Angeles Times (Apr 2026); The New York Times via Moneywise (2026); Hypebeast and Comic Basics (Oct 2026)
Photos: y entonces, Mike J Maguire, Shook Photos, Kjmagnuson, State Library Victoria, Rennett Stowe, superiphi, blondinrikard (CC BY 2.0, Flickr); Russell Lee, Library of Congress (public domain)
tags: why is movie theater popcorn so expensive
first_comment: Be honest: do you sneak snacks into the movies, or pay for the popcorn? 🍿

scenes.say: Theaters are selling a {$90|ninety dollar} Godzilla popcorn bucket. And they need you to buy it.
scenes.source: Hypebeast Oct 2026; Comic Basics Oct 2026; Alamo Drafthouse pre-order listing

scenes.say: Because when a blockbuster hits, the studio takes more than half of every ticket.
scenes.source: AMC 10-Q Q2 2025 (US film exhibition costs 54.4% of admissions); NBC News/CNBC 2015 (Disney 60%+ on Force Awakens)

scenes.say: But on snacks, AMC keeps about {82¢|eighty two cents} of every dollar after paying for the food.
scenes.source: AMC 2025 annual report (US food and beverage costs 18.1% of F&B revenues); AMC 10-Q Q2 2025

scenes.say: Funny thing is, theaters used to ban popcorn.
scenes.source: Smithsonian Magazine (Andrew F. Smith, Popped Culture); Reader's Digest

scenes.say: In the {1920s|nineteen twenties}, fancy movie palaces didn't want it crunching into their carpets.
Then the Great Depression hit. And a bag of popcorn cost just {5–10¢|five to ten cents}.
Theaters that started selling snacks survived. A lot of the ones that refused didn't.
scenes.source: Smithsonian Magazine (Andrew F. Smith); Snopes/Yahoo fact check 2024

scenes.say: By {1945|nineteen forty five}, over half the popcorn eaten in America was eaten at the movies.
In {2023|twenty twenty three}, AMC sold collectible buckets for {9|nine} movies. This year, more than {40|forty}.
scenes.source: Los Angeles Times, Apr 6 2026 (Iris Kwok); LA Times summary via Pulse

scenes.say: AMC made {$54 MILLION|fifty four million dollars} on movie merch in {2023|twenty twenty three}. This year, it expects about {$100 MILLION|a hundred million}.
scenes.source: The Wrap 2024 and LA Times Apr 2026 ($54M); The New York Times via Moneywise 2026 (~$100M)

scenes.say: Popcorn kept the lights on during the Depression. And it's still keeping them on. Which is exactly why
scenes.source: LA Times Apr 2026 (popcorn as a lifeline for movie palaces); AMC 2025 annual report
